issue.close_reason: Investigation complete. Determined that --profile flag should NOT be supported on sync flush-only. Implementation is correct (properly rejects the flag), but documentation at docs/plan/plan.md:845 incorrectly shows [--profile P] as a supported option. Recommendation document produced at notes/beadrs-4840ec09-recommendation.md with full analysis and required documentation fix.
issue.description:
Investigate the --profile flag on sync flush-only command. Determine if the flag should be supported or removed from help text. The SyncFlushOptions struct currently has no profile field. This task is to determine the correct behavior without making changes yet.

Acceptance criteria:
- Document the intended behavior for --profile on flush-only
- Identify all locations where profile is referenced in relation to flush-only
- Determine whether profile should be user-selectable for flush-only
- Produce a recommendation document
issue.notes:
Investigation complete. Summary:

**Current Status**: Implementation is CORRECT - SyncFlushOptions has no profile field and properly rejects --profile with exit code 2.

**Key Finding**: --profile only exists on sync import-only (not flush-only) because:
- flush-only: database → checkpoint (always native-v1 format)
- import-only: checkpoint → database (may be needle-v1, native-v1, etc.)

**Documentation Issue Found**: docs/plan/plan.md line 845 incorrectly shows [--profile P] as supported. This contradicts the spec at line 1594 which states 'sync --flush-only rejects every other profile'.

**Action Required**: Update plan.md line 845 to remove [--profile P] from the command specification.

**Test Coverage**: test_sync_flush_only_rejects_invalid_profile validates proper rejection (exit code 2, 'unexpected argument --profile').

**Detailed recommendation**: See notes/beadrs-4840ec09-recommendation.md for complete analysis with evidence from code, tests, and documentation.
issue.title: Investigate sync flush-only --profile flag behavior

issue.close_reason:
Implemented R037: Command errors that name the remedy

- Added hidden flags to clap definitions for common near-miss arguments (update --title, --description, --priority, --issue-type, --label; close --body; create --status, --notes)
- Added validation logic in command handlers to detect these flags and show remediation messages that state the domain rule and provide specific remedies
- Updated conformance tests to assert the remedy text, not merely nonzero exit codes
- All 10 R037 conformance tests passing

No currently-rejected invocations become accepted. No semantics changed. This is message quality only.
issue.description:
Where a command rejects an argument a competent operator would expect to work, state the domain rule and the remedy instead of surfacing a bare parser error. Generalizes the standard `release` already sets when it refuses an assigned open issue with "use 'update --clear-assignee' instead".

Verified against the shipped CLI 2026-08-16:

  bead update <id> --title "x"  -> error: unexpected argument '--title' found
                                   tip: to pass '--title' as a value, use '-- --title'
  bead close <id> --body "x"    -> error: unexpected argument '--body' found
                                   tip: to pass '--body' as a value, use '-- --body'

Both are actively misleading: the tip proposes escaping the flag as a positional value, which is never the intent and produces a second confusing failure if followed. Neither states the actual rule. Both are load-bearing enough that downstream environment documentation carries explicit warnings about them.

No currently-rejected invocation becomes accepted. No semantics change. This is message quality only.

Acceptance:
- fields immutable after create (title, description, priority, issue-type) produce an error naming the rule and any supported alternative, e.g. label add|remove for labels
- close --body names --reason
- near-miss handling is bounded to flags that exist on sibling commands, not general fuzzy matching
- conformance scenarios assert the remedy text, not merely a nonzero exit, so the affordance cannot regress to a parser default

Refs: ADR-007; plan section 5 command and process contract; plan section 12 R037.
issue.title: R037: Command errors that name the remedy

issue.description:
ADR-005 records as a drawback that a deliberately parked, assigned issue is indistinguishable from worker residue, so an operator with real reservations would learn to ignore the doctor warning. Add an operator-set 'intentionally held' marker with a public CLI flag/command, an audit event, and a field-guide entry, which suppresses the doctor ready_frontier warning for that issue only. It must not change claim eligibility (a marked assigned open issue stays out of the frontier). Tests: marked issues stop warning but remain unclaimable, and the marker survives `update`/`reopen` round trips and checkpoint publication.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Allow marking an assignment as intentionally held to silence the ready-frontier warning

issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted, 2026-08-12) decides that authors declare check relationships via a third dependency kind `verifies`, and that inversion of verification gates is diagnosed structurally from that declaration — reported, never rejected at insert time, and never inferred from issue titles. The ADR defers it to 'post-0.1 item R025' and no open bead tracks it. Work needed: extend the dependency schema and CLI to accept the `verifies` kind, add the advisory inversion diagnostic (a `blocks` edge whose blocker `verifies` its target), surface it alongside the R021/R023 `why` explanation, cover round-trip through the checkpoint and unknown-field preservation, add concurrency tests for edge insertion (same transaction discipline as §3.4 cycle rejection), and document the kind in help/schema/capabilities.

Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Implement the `verifies` dependency kind and inverted-gate diagnosis (R025)

issue.description:
ADR-004 requires a pinned MSRV verification lane in bead-rs-ci — `cargo +1.85 check --all-targets`, with the lane's toolchain matching Cargo.toml's rust-version and drift between them a CI failure — precisely because the declared floor was measured as 'honest today by luck, not by verification'. No open bead tracks this and no supplied doc records it as done, unlike the dependency refresh which got a dated 2026-08-22 completion note. First step: confirm whether the lane already exists in the applied WorkflowTemplate (kubectl read-only against iad-ci) before writing anything; if absent, add the step to the template in declarative-config/k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, own the change on a bead in this repo per the deployment-bead ownership rule, add a drift assertion against rust-version, and record one green run proving the 1.85 floor compiles against the current lockfile.
